active_goal.objective: Ship a production-ready, self-contained Rust BORSUK ANN library on S3/blob storage that beats BOTH S3 Vectors and Turbopuffer at equal or better recall on matched end-to-end p90/p95 latency and throughput per total dollar. This is a product goal, not a report. Support incremental insert/update/delete, authenticated generation-pinned publication and reads, bounded RAM/cache/concurrency, restart/recovery, and in-process automatic or callable compaction/GC; require no separate maintenance instance. Preserve current V282 on-demand SQ8 work and live jobs; do not duplicate consultations or paid runs. Opus 5.5 estimates the current PQ64 plus f32 summary/unit router at 184 resident bytes per row, or about 18.4 GB at 100M D768, before old-generation pinning. This is a projection, not a measurement. Reconcile prior V139/V146/V149/V150 centroid-page failures and the completed Fable review before choosing any new arm; do not repeat a known failure. Predeclare a feasible 100M RAM, GET, byte, p90 and cost envelope. Prefer a small resident router and one parallel S3 fetch wave, but choose memory versus quality from a measured Pareto curve, not an arbitrary 2 GB cap. Candidate design: balanced hierarchical semantic cells with physical locality and boundary coverage; scan small SQ8 leaves, split skewed/diffuse leaves, use local compressed indexing only where measured cell-specific gains justify it. Avoid S3 graph pointer chasing and full-vector/full-graph hydration. First run the cheapest distinct paired 100k D768 cosine k100 falsifier on ReLAION and CoHere against unchanged V282, decomposing exact-GT loss into router, selected-cell coverage, local index and SQ8 quantization and counting GETs, bytes, RAM and route CPU. Use V282 98% mean recall@100, p05 95, 32 GET and 16 MiB caps unless a redesign is predeclared; kill weak arms early. Freeze a winner for fresh 1M cold HTTP, then 10M and 100M scale. Measure p50/p90/p95/p99, QPS, RSS including generation swap, physical S3 requests/bytes/retries/errors, build and incremental-maintenance cost, total lifecycle cost and failure recovery. Compare competitors on identical corpus, query split, metric, k, filters, cache state, region and concurrency; if only published targets are available, cite date/configuration and label mismatches, never claim a measured win. When a gate fails, redesign routing, layout, quantization or fetch schedule with one causal change per experiment. Unreleased formats need no backward compatibility. Push code, tests, receipts and a concise decision table to BORSUK main. Within 24 hours deliver one substantive object-native library increment and a falsifiable next gate, then continue until the product works.

Candidate `9853e133` is a defensible consumed-panel falsifier, but remains unqualified. I found two validation gaps and one material integration-test gap.

1. **P1 — “Frozen original authority” does not bind historical truth.**  
   The seal comparison authenticates roots and requests at [fine_sq8_groups.rs:3331](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-fixed-sq4-native-refinement/crates/borsuk/src/fine_sq8_groups.rs:3331). Truth validation accepts the new config’s hash and checks its geometry and IDs; the authority flag at [line 3584](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-fixed-sq4-native-refinement/crates/borsuk/src/fine_sq8_groups.rs:3584) omits truth entirely. Consequently, replacement truth with an updated config hash can still receive historical-authority status.

   **Action:** bind both truth hashes to the [original authenticated paired config](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-prod-ready-v9/docs/research/performance-architecture-20260930/semantic-1m/fine-sq8-groups/paired100k/a0002/screen/fine/measurement/paired-fine-config.json:1), without opening truth early. Add a replacement-truth rejection check. If the parent owns this binding externally, its admission receipt must demonstrate it; `admit_survival` alone does not.

2. **P2 — Original SQ8 growth after transcoding escapes validation.**  
   Original EOF is checked at [line 3024](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-fixed-sq4-native-refinement/crates/borsuk/src/fine_sq8_groups.rs:3024). Subsequent scoring reads authenticated ranges from the retained descriptor at [line 3194](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-fixed-sq4-native-refinement/crates/borsuk/src/fine_sq8_groups.rs:3194), while pre-truth closure reauthentication checks the new payloads at [line 3498](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-fixed-sq4-native-refinement/crates/borsuk/src/fine_sq8_groups.rs:3498). Appending to an original between those stages leaves fetched group hashes valid and goes undetected.

   **Action:** recheck exact EOF on both retained originals before truth acquisition. Test growth after successful transcode. This concerns artifact validation; it does not demonstrate biased recall.

3. **Integration evidence gap — Neither 128-query fixture exercises range coalescence.**  
   Both fixtures contain 135 rows: only nine groups. Thus their 32-range and 256-range covers cannot differ. The genuine build fixture also uses repeated queries and one-hot vectors whose codes collapse to zero under this codec. See [the pipeline test](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-fixed-sq4-native-refinement/crates/borsuk/src/bin/hierarchical_semantic_cells.rs:1813), [its source fixture](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-fixed-sq4-native-refinement/crates/borsuk/src/bin/hierarchical_semantic_cells.rs:2167), and [the library pipeline fixture](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-fixed-sq4-native-refinement/crates/borsuk/src/fine_sq8_groups.rs:4195).

   **Action:** add one bounded pipeline case with more than 32 disjoint selected groups, nontrivial nibble levels, and distinct queries. Assert that added incidental rows participate in both scoring arms and check expected rankings. The standalone cover test establishes geometry but cannot catch a pipeline accidentally scoring the old population.

The causal comparison itself is sound. Both arms receive identical expanded ranges, query normalization matches the corrected contract, reconstructed norms are recomputed sequentially, and the historical baseline remains separate. Static inspection found no codec/scorer mismatch.

Three scientific limitations remain:

- **Coverage containment does not imply returned-recall improvement.** Additional rows can displace true neighbors under approximate SQ8 scores. Report reference-minus-baseline and SQ4-minus-reference separately; the existing outputs support this decomposition.
- **The scorer measures reconstructed squared L2.** Quantization changes database norms, so this is an approximation to original cosine retrieval, not exact cosine on reconstructed vectors. Recomputing norms is correct for the frozen arm. The normalized-vector equivalence requires normalized database vectors too. [Faiss metric documentation](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/wiki/MetricType-and-distances)
- **Thirty-two ranges do not establish lower cost or faster serving.** Recalculating the closed cover metadata gives 2.32×/2.43× more scored rows and 18%/23% more payload bytes for ReLAION/CoHere. The diagnostic additionally expands records and executes two reference arms; its whole-process time cannot represent candidate serving latency.

Prior art narrows the interpretation of failure. Faiss supports trained SQ4 and transformed codecs; RaBitQ changes the representation and distance estimator; DiskANN places graph neighborhoods and full vectors on SSD while retaining compressed vectors in memory. A failure here rejects **nearest-17 refinement with this frozen layout**, not four-bit quantization generally. These alternatives would require separate protocols, not changes to this arm. [Faiss codecs](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/wiki/Vector-codecs), [RaBitQ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09913), [DiskANN](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2019/file/09853c7fb1d3f8ee67a61b6bf4a7f8e6-Paper.pdf)

I verified the clean candidate revision, both contract source hashes, and `git diff --check`. Native compilation, tests, actual failure receipts, Clippy, complete workspace test-build, observed resource limits, and measured SQ4 recall remain **UNRUN**. Keep the fixed scientific limits unchanged; setup or qualification failures remain INVALID.

No files, goal, or worker were changed. No Cargo or cloud execution was performed.

Independent binary32 emulation found **zero differences across its 256 rows plus the wrapper’s 135 rows** when replacing sequential f32 norm arithmetic with f64 arithmetic followed by an f32 cast.

   A distinguishing fixture is `low=[0.1,0.2,0.3]`, `step=[0.01,0.02,0.03]`, reconstructed codes `[17,34,51]`: sequential norm bits are `0x40864744`; wider arithmetic produces `0x40864745`.

   **Fix:** add that exact-bit witness and confirm the forbidden implementation fails it. Current production encoding uses the required sequential f32 arithmetic; this is a regression-test gap.

The receipt loses that distinction, the freeze pin, and available resource counters.

   **Fix:** retain bounded failure context—stage, scored-query count, truth-open state, published bytes, and freeze identity—while keeping `INVALID` and nonzero exit. Extend the existing fault test to assert these facts.
